name: workflow-conversion
description: Convert LLM-orchestrated pipeline prompts (e.g., do.md, fix.md) to deterministic Claude Code JS Workflow scripts (.wf.js). Eliminates non-deterministic LLM routing in favor of JS control flow with typed subagent schemas.
when_to_use: When an existing prompt-based pipeline has complex branching, retries, or multi-phase state handoffs that would benefit from deterministic JS orchestration. Especially when token cost of LLM-orchestrated routing is a concern or when subagent schemas need strict validation.
workflow_sequences: Read existing .md prompt → identify phases and decision branches → write .wf.js with runStep/runSubagent → define typed schema constants → write tests in tests/workflows/ → run_quality_gate()
For each subagent: read cursor-agents/*.md → trim to ≤30 lines → keep structured output schema → sync_cursor_agents() → run_quality_gate()
example_invocations: Convert fix.md (LLM routing) to fix.wf.js: extract Branch A/B/C logic into JS switch, define QUALITY_SCHEMA/TESTS_SCHEMA, write 84 structural tests
Convert do.md to do.wf.js: selection phase → implementation loop → finalize, 476 lines, 69 tests
Trim implement-code.md from 80 lines to ≤30 lines: remove MCP tool prose, keep numbered steps with expected output fields
troubleshooting_tips: Cross-check each rewrite against schema constants in .wf.js files — missing a required structured output field causes silent JS validation failures at runtime.
After trimming cursor-agent .md files, run sync_cursor_agents() to propagate changes to .claude/agents/ — stale copies break Claude Code CLI invocations.
Keep all decision branch labels (Branch A/B/C) even as one-liners — removing them causes silent misbehavior in edge cases.
To pass failure context inline: extract prior gate errors in the JS orchestrator and inject them into the agent prompt string; agents can skip their first gate call if prior_errors is populated.
